assessment: Read 1-154; static review only. Traced factory dispatch, applied/state LiveData, root apply/error propagation and passive VPN refresh. The VPN branch samples establishment without preparing or starting a service. Concrete refresh status messages inspected contain no hostname or source URL. Static review. Tunnel status is a point-in-time observation; did not exercise root installation, VPN ownership or platform callbacks. Source-only follow-up: P2 L62-70,97-104: UNDEFINED returns an applied receipt. Handle UNDEFINED explicitly as not applied or unsupported.

Read 1-148; static review only. Traced explicit prepare/start versus passive cache refresh, stop, volatile cache replacement and concurrent lookups. An outstanding lookup can finish on its retired cache but cannot populate the replacement. DNS recording defaults off; this class keeps at most 1000 distinct names in memory, synchronizes changes and returns a copy. Static review; no live DNS, device or scheduler tests. Explicit apply posts start acceptance, not proof of establishment; the Sources caller separately checks the tunnel. Reporting concerns in this model, not all app logging. Source-only follow-up: P2 L43-48,72-90,133-146 (integration): invalidation is per instance but application-level model creation is unsynchronized. Ensure a single safely published model per method so the live DNS proxy and refresh operate on the same cache.

Read 1-537; static review only. L106-236: update label and navigation, help intent, download-dialog navigation, rotation and Back. L241-324: French-to-English rendering without republishing, refresh text across recreation, and visibility of a newer status after acknowledgement. Manifest and errors are injected (L326-383); these tests do not exercise fetching or failure detection. Source-only follow-up: L267-286: the protection-off test checks a false return and visible text, not whether VPN start was requested or protection remained off. A delayed start could pass. L155-171: Sources navigation and a null error are checked, but the test never returns Home to check for replay.

Read 1-421; static review only. L105-124, L251-274, L348-363, L383-394: invokes the toolbar handler, observes installing text while retrieval is held, releases the fixture to sync seeded rows, then checks an apply was recorded and the test host resolves as blocked. Recording models substitute for remote retrieval and real protection. L183-191 and L208-220 wait for at least one call, not exactly one. Source-only follow-up: L211-216, L388-393: the waiter reads failure before applyCount. An early apply can record its failure and increment between those reads; a later successful DB sync can satisfy L119-124. Check the failure after observing completion. L91-101, L107-109: teardown releases but does not join a pending update before DB reset, and the launched scenario is never closed.

Read 1-68; static review only. L16-45: checks literal menu ID/title, English copy, update-all dispatch, receipt/apply tokens and the installing-message resource reference in repository files. Source-text contract only; does not execute Android code or parse XML/Java. Formatting-only changes can also fail the checks. Source-only follow-up: L26-28, L33-45: independent contains checks do not bind the title to the menu item, or apply() to the successful-receipt branch. Moving apply() outside the guard while retaining all strings can still pass.

Read 1-579; static review only. L316-424: legacy service/network evidence and API 31 UID matching. L444-559: consent, rejected launches, cache invalidation and passive refresh. The six passive cases check status, cache lookups, publications and zero prepare/launch/heartbeat calls. Host-side production logic with platform doubles, synchronous LiveData and ID-only strings (L27-49, L124, L206-218); no device lifecycle or real tunnel. Source-only follow-up: L83-85, L125-129, L325-328: the Intent constructor drops the target class and the launch stub always returns the VPN component on acceptance. A START command sent to the wrong service can pass. L402-410: both managers are absent for the final check, so it does not isolate missing connectivity with an otherwise valid service.
